title: Codon Chart: Test Yourself on All 64 Codons (RNA & DNA)
description: All 64 RNA and DNA codons in one chart, with the start codon, the three stops and amino acid classes marked, plus a 7-question self-test on reading it.
intro: Seven questions on the codons people misread most, each answered straight from the chart above with a one-line reason.

questions.q: Which of these RNA codons ends translation instead of adding an amino acid?
questions.why: UGA is a stop codon, while UGG differs from it by one base and codes tryptophan, so the two are easy to swap.

questions.q: Which set lists all three stop codons of the standard RNA code?
questions.why: Only UAA, UAG and UGA carry no amino acid; UGG is tryptophan, UGC is cysteine and AUG is the start codon.

questions.q: Which RNA codon is both the start signal and the codon for methionine?
questions.why: AUG sets the reading frame at the beginning and still puts methionine into the chain wherever else it appears.
questions.source: table: AUG -> M (Met), marked Start on the chart

questions.q: The RNA codons ACU, ACC, ACA and ACG all give threonine. Which base can change without changing the amino acid?
questions.why: Those four codons differ only at the third position, the wobble base, which is where most of the code's degeneracy sits.
questions.source: table: ACU -> T, ACC -> T, ACA -> T, ACG -> T (Thr)

questions.q: Counting RNA codons in the chart, which of these amino acids has six of them?
questions.why: Leucine, serine and arginine each have six codons, while methionine and tryptophan have only one, so a single change always alters them.
questions.source: table: UUA, UUG, CUU, CUC, CUA, CUG -> L (Leu); CAU, CAC -> H; CAA, CAG -> Q; AUG -> M

questions.q: A DNA coding-strand triplet reads TAC. Rewrite it as RNA and look it up: what does the chart give?
questions.why: DNA's T becomes RNA's U, so TAC is the codon UAC, which is tyrosine, not the stop codon UAA.
questions.source: table: UAC -> Y (Tyr); UAA -> * (Stop); CAC -> H (His); AAC -> N (Asn)

questions.q: An mRNA codon reads CAG from 5-prime to 3-prime. Read backwards as GAC, which amino acid does the chart give?
questions.why: CAG is glutamine but GAC is aspartate, so reading a codon in the wrong direction lands on a different amino acid entirely.
